NINTENDO 3DS

Build your movie menu

Package your MOFLEX movies, episode menu and artwork into a CIA locally, using your own compatible player template.

1. Select your MOFLEX files

Your movies stay on your device. No video data is uploaded or embedded in the project JSON.

Choose 1–27 MOFLEX files, then arrange their order.

    2. HOME Menu information

    Choose a title ID that is not already installed. You must supply artwork files alongside the exported project when packaging.

    3. Build a CIA

    Select a legally obtained, decrypted VidInjector collection-player CIA for 1–27 episodes. A single-movie player template supports one movie. The player and menu layout are preserved. Movie data is read in bounded chunks. The finished file must fit FAT32. PNG, BMP and JPG icons and episode thumbnails are converted locally. Banner images update the compatible template model. Optional mono/stereo PCM16 WAV audio at 8–48 kHz is limited to 10 seconds. Prepared CBMD banners remain supported.

    Splitting preserves episode order and reserves the template size plus 64 MiB per part for packaging overhead. Parts use consecutive title IDs starting with your chosen ID. Each completed CIA is checked against FAT32. Allow multiple downloads when prompted.

    Uses private browser storage and keeps the files available after reload until deleted or browser storage is cleared.

    Save project settings

    Save the episode order and settings as a native-compatible JSON project. The Build CIA button uses your selected local template. You can also use the JSON project with the native builder. No account, server, or paid API is required.

    Add movies and complete the fields above.

    Put the project JSON, your original MOFLEX files, and any selected icon/banner assets in the same folder. Run:

    python3 native/cia_builder.py build project.json movie.cia --backend /path/to/VidInjector9002-CLI

    The native builder strips SUPER MOFLEX extras before packaging for the original Nintendo player, checks the title ID, FAT32 limits and CIA content hashes. Actual console installation and playback still require testing.
